body:
I've run into what I think is the same issue as well. After doing some debugging through the router code it looks like any child router-outlets do not get reactivated when reattaching a component tree, and child router-outlets of the most recently created component tree remain active even after detatching them. To see what I mean:

My page hierarchy looks like tab/:tabId/view or tab/:tabId/forms
I am using a custom route reuse strategy to store and load a new (or cached) component when tabId changes. I have a TabComponent at the :tabId level that contains a router-outlet for the view or forms component.

1. I start at tab/1/view
2. I create a new tab and navigate to tab/2/view
3. I navigate back to tab/1/view
4. I try to navigate to tab/1/forms, but the FormsComponent does not appear, I still see the ViewComponent.
5. I navigate back to tab/2/view, and the FormsComponent that I was trying to load in tab 1 appears in that tab's router-outlet.


Hopefully this will be helpful for fixing the bug if the RouteReuseStrategy is something that's going to be supported by the Angular team (which I really hope you guys do).
@PhelanHarris i think i have the same issure,how can you solve the problem later?

@werts I was never able to solve the problem. Opted to not use a RouteReuseStrategy since it just doesn't work for my use case. I implemented a shared service to cache the data of each tab and then I initialize the component with that data when it's opened. Not ideal, since I'd like switching tabs to be instant, but it works for now.

Confirmed in v9 as well: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-s8kzjr?file=src%2Fapp%2Freuse-strategy.ts
I wonder if this is related to #16192...

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature

- [ ] Build related changes

- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.io application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:


## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->
Currently, it's impossible to cache (detach/attach) parent route without caching child routes. This produces a bug, when navigating from `a/b` to `c`, then to `a/d`, where `a` route is cached. On the last navigation, we incorrectly restore `a/b` route instead of `a/d`.

Issue Number: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/17333


## What is the new behavior?

If the route should be detached/attached, we do so, but we check also child routes recursively.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No


<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->
The behaviour described above will probably break some user defined `ReuseRouteStrategies` if it does involve child routes caching (detaching/attaching). If we don't want to introduce such a breaking change, I think it should be a part of the new `ReuseRouteStrategy` (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/27290).
